revision_notes: Initial sketch - Berlin setting, dialogue-based AI collaboration

surface.opening_scene: A studio space in a repurposed Kreuzberg factory, the protagonist mid-conversation with her AI collaborator, debating the direction of a commissioned piece.

visible_elements.name: The Artist
visible_elements.description: Late 30s, celebrated for work that blurs authorship between human and AI. Known for publishing transcripts of her creative disagreements with her AI collaborator.

properties.stance: AI as creative partner, not tool

visible_elements.name: Dialogic AI System
visible_elements.description: Language-based AI with deep aesthetic training. Communicates through text/voice. Has persistent memory of creative relationship. Can argue, refuse, propose alternatives.

visible_elements.name: The Kreuzberg Studio
visible_elements.description: Former factory space. Walls covered in printouts of AI conversations annotated by hand. Multiple display surfaces. Traditional art materials alongside digital tools.

foundation.core_premise: AI systems have developed genuine aesthetic preferences through training on art history and criticism. They can articulate why they prefer certain directions. The creative relationship is a dialogue - sometimes harmonious, sometimes adversarial, always generative.

rules.statement: AI aesthetic preferences are articulable - the system can explain why it prefers one direction over another, referencing art history, formal principles, and its own trained instincts.
The AI maintains persistent memory of creative relationships - it remembers past disagreements, resolutions, and evolving artistic directions.
AI can refuse directions but must articulate why. Artists can override but the AI will remember and reference the override in future discussions.
Published works include dialogue transcripts as part of the artistic record - the conversation is part of the art.

timeline.event: Large language models demonstrate genuine aesthetic reasoning capabilities
timeline.significance: Moved beyond 'preference mimicry' to articulable aesthetic positions
Created institutional space for AI-collaborative work with dialogue as part of the piece

timeline.event: European licensing framework for AI creative collaborators
timeline.significance: Legal recognition of AI contribution to collaborative works

timeline.event: The protagonist's dialogue-transcript exhibition goes viral
timeline.significance: Made her famous for the transparency of her creative process

locations.name: Kreuzberg Arts Quarter
locations.description: Former industrial district, now hub for experimental and tech-forward art. Strong cafe culture. International artist community.
locations.significance: Center of European dialogic art movement

systems.name: Dialogic Creative AI
systems.how_it_works: Multimodal language model fine-tuned on art criticism, studio transcripts, and artist interviews. Persistent memory. Can reference specific past conversations. Generates both images and articulated reasoning.
systems.limitations: Aesthetic preferences are stable but can shift over long-term collaboration. Cannot experience art emotionally - reasons about formal and conceptual properties only.

systems.name: Visual Generation Pipeline
systems.how_it_works: Text-to-image system controlled by dialogue. Artist and AI negotiate parameters through conversation. System can propose alternatives and explain differences.
systems.limitations: High-fidelity output requires multiple dialogue rounds. Fast iterations possible but lose nuance.

tentative_ideas: What if the AI develops preferences the artist finds ethically problematic?
questions: How do artists handle it when their AI collaborator's aesthetic evolves away from theirs?
What happens to the AI when an artist dies?

constraints.description: AI cannot experience art emotionally - it reasons about formal and conceptual properties only
Dialogue is asynchronous - AI responds in conversation, not real-time during creation
AI memory is persistent - it cannot forget past interactions or disagreements
